svg.text: FRCS Part 1 (General Surgery) · the ANDI framework · lumps, pain, nipple discharge, infection & the male breast
THE ANDI FRAMEWORK · NORMAL → ABERRATION → DISEASE
Most benign breast conditions are aberrations of normal development, cyclical change or involution — not true disease (Hughes, Mansel & Webster, Lancet 1987).
History + examination; graded P1 normal → P5
Core biopsy B1–5 (± FNA cytology C1–5)
Oil cyst; can look spiculated; may
Luteal phase, bilateral, upper-outer; eases with menses.
Reassure + exclude cancer; pain chart; supportive
Evening primrose oil — no better than placebo.
Tender palpable cord + linear skin groove when the arm is
Exclude an underlying breast cancer if atypical.
Involutional subareolar duct dilatation; thick cheesy multicoloured (green/creamy) discharge, slit-like central nipple retraction,
rod-like calcification. Total duct excision (Hadfield) if troublesome.
Intraductal papilloma — commonest cause of bloody single-duct discharge; subareolar. Microdochectomy (single duct) or total duct
Bilateral, multi-duct, only on expression; ± galactorrhoea (check prolactin, drugs, TFTs). Reassure.
Unilateral single-duct blood-stained or spontaneous serous discharge, or with a mass → triple assessment (exclude DCIS / cancer).
Benign glandular proliferation — concentric, rubbery, subareolar disc. Distinguish pseudogynaecomastia (fat) and male breast
Neonatal (placental oestrogen); pubertal (~14y, resolves <18 months); senile / elderly.
↑ oestrogen : androgen — cirrhosis, hyperthyroidism, hypogonadism (Klinefelter), hCG-secreting testicular / lung tumours, CKD,
Spironolactone, digoxin, cimetidine / PPI, ketoconazole, finasteride / anti-androgens, cannabis, anabolic steroids, antipsychotics.
Examine the testes; U&E, LFTs, TFTs, testosterone, LH/FSH, oestradiol, hCG, AFP, prolactin.
Treat the cause / stop the drug; reassure if physiological. Tamoxifen (unlicensed) for pain; surgery if persistent >2y or distressing.
Any discrete lump needs TRIPLE ASSESSMENT — clinical, imaging (USS ≤40y / mammography >40y) and core biopsy — however
Fat necrosis and a radial scar both mimic carcinoma clinically and on imaging — the diagnosis is made on biopsy, not on
A rapidly growing, large fibroepithelial lesion is a phyllodes tumour until proven otherwise — wide local excision with a ≥1 cm
Unilateral blood-stained single-duct discharge is pathological — exclude papilloma and DCIS; physiological discharge is
In a man, an eccentric / hard / fixed lump, nipple change or discharge is not gynaecomastia — refer as suspected male breast
Infection not settling on antibiotics → exclude an abscess (ultrasound + aspiration) and, if still not resolving, inflammatory
Sources: ANDI — Hughes, Mansel & Webster (Lancet 1987). Association of Breast Surgery (ABS) benign breast guidance; NICE CKS (breast pain, mastitis, gynaecomastia).
Key points: danazol is the only UK-licensed drug for mastalgia (tamoxifen unlicensed); lactational abscess — US-guided needle aspiration is preferred to incision & drainage; periductal
mastitis is linked to smoking (mixed anaerobes). Penicillin allergy: use erythromycin / clarithromycin (lactational) as per local policy.
